title: Half-Open Range Ambiguity (`stop` vs `end`)
pattern: An inclusive/exclusive (half-open) range representation where the exclusive upper limit is named `stop` instead of `end`, or the inclusive lower limit is named `start` instead of `begin`.
why_bad: English does not have a succinct word for "just past the last value." Using non-idiomatic terms like `stop` for half-open ranges obscures the exclusive nature of the upper boundary. Using `begin`/`end` is the industry-standard idiom for inclusive/exclusive slices.
detection: Match structs or functions defining ranges with `begin` and `stop` or `start` and `end` inconsistently.
counterexample:
Using standard, idiomatic pairs for half-open intervals:
```rust
struct EventRange {
    begin: u64,
    end: u64, // end is conventionally exclusive here
}
```
source: *The Art of Readable Code* by Dustin Boswell and Trevor Foucher (Chapter 3, pp. 26-27).
